cell-theory.question: The statement 'all cells arise from pre-existing cells' forms part of the…
cell-theory.explanation: This is Virchow's contribution to Cell Theory: every cell comes from a cell that already existed.

cell-theory.question: A cell's small size is mainly an advantage because it…
options: increases its surface area to volume ratio for efficient exchange
reduces the amount of DNA needed
cell-theory.explanation: A high surface-area-to-volume ratio lets small cells exchange materials with their surroundings efficiently.

cell-theory.question: Which of the following best distinguishes a light microscope from an electron microscope?
options: A light microscope allows viewing of living specimens while an electron microscope does not
An electron microscope uses light rays
A light microscope has a higher magnification than an electron microscope
cell-theory.explanation: Light microscopes can view living specimens; electron microscopes require a vacuum and cannot.

cell-organelles.question: Which organelle is correctly matched with its function?
cell-organelles.explanation: The nucleus controls the cell's activities. The other pairings are incorrect.

cell-organelles.question: The organelle responsible for packaging and modifying proteins before they leave the cell is the…
cell-organelles.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins into vesicles for transport.

cell-organelles.question: Aerobic respiration mainly occurs in the…
cell-organelles.explanation: The mitochondrion is the main site of aerobic respiration and ATP production.

plant-vs-animal.question: One structural feature found in plant cells but absent in animal cells is the…
plant-vs-animal.explanation: The cellulose cell wall is present in plant cells and absent in animal cells.

plant-vs-animal.question: Chloroplasts are found in…
plant-vs-animal.explanation: Chloroplasts, needed for photosynthesis, are found only in plant cells (their green parts).

plant-vs-animal.question: The large central vacuole in a mature plant cell mainly functions to…
plant-vs-animal.explanation: The large permanent vacuole maintains turgor pressure, keeping the plant firm and supported.

prokaryote-vs-eukaryote.question: A prokaryotic cell differs from a eukaryotic cell mainly in that it…
prokaryote-vs-eukaryote.explanation: The defining difference is the absence of a true, membrane-bound nucleus in prokaryotic cells.

prokaryote-vs-eukaryote.question: Which of these is an example of a prokaryotic organism?
prokaryote-vs-eukaryote.explanation: Escherichia coli is a bacterium, making it a prokaryotic organism; the others are eukaryotic.

prokaryote-vs-eukaryote.question: Prokaryotic organisms typically reproduce by…
prokaryote-vs-eukaryote.explanation: Prokaryotes reproduce mainly by binary fission, a simple splitting into two.

levels-of-organisation.question: Arrange the following in order of increasing complexity: organ, cell, tissue.
levels-of-organisation.explanation: The correct increasing order of organisation is cell, then tissue, then organ.

levels-of-organisation.question: A group of similar cells performing the same function is called a…
levels-of-organisation.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing the same function.

levels-of-organisation.question: The digestive system is an example of a(n)…
levels-of-organisation.explanation: The digestive system is an organ system: several organs (mouth, stomach, intestines) working together.

cell-cycle-chromosomes.question: The chromosome number in the body cells of an organism is described as
cell-cycle-chromosomes.explanation: Body (somatic) cells carry two full sets of chromosomes — the diploid number.

cell-cycle-chromosomes.question: A structure formed by two sister chromatids joined at a centromere is called a
cell-cycle-chromosomes.explanation: After DNA replication, a chromosome consists of two sister chromatids joined at a centromere.

mitosis.question: The stage of mitosis during which chromosomes align at the equator of the cell is
mitosis.explanation: Metaphase is the alignment stage, allowing spindle fibres to attach to every centromere.

mitosis.question: Mitosis results in the formation of
options: one diploid and one haploid cell
mitosis.explanation: Mitosis produces 2 daughter cells, diploid and genetically identical to the parent.

meiosis.question: Meiosis is best described as a type of cell division that produces
options: four haploid cells from one diploid cell
two diploid cells from one diploid cell
two haploid cells from one haploid cell
one diploid cell from two haploid cells
meiosis.explanation: Meiosis's two divisions turn one diploid cell into four haploid cells.

meiosis.question: The exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes during meiosis is known as
meiosis.explanation: Crossing over is the swap of equivalent DNA sections between paired homologous chromosomes.
